extra.message: Using variable interpolation `${{...}}` with `github` context data in a `run:` step could allow an attacker to inject their own code into the runner. This would allow them to steal secrets and code. `github` context data can have arbitrary user input and should be treated as untrusted. Instead, use an intermediate environment variable with `env:` to store the data and use the environment variable in the `run:` script. Be sure to use double-quotes the environment variable, like this: "$ENVVAR".

extra.message: Redirect target derives from a request-controlled value with no host allowlist — a classic open-redirect primitive for phishing (and SSRF-shaped if fetched server-side). SCOPE OF THIS CHECK (#1342), so its silence elsewhere is not read as a clean bill of health: it follows the value within this file only. A host allowlist enforced elsewhere — in shared middleware, a route wrapper, or a helper the value passes through — is not something this rule reads, so confirm no such guard runs before treating this as unmitigated. A host allowlist that rejects by THROWING is recognised (#1248) only when no `try` follows the `new URL(...)` projection in the same scope, so a correct guard whose URL parse is itself wrapped in try/catch is reported here rather than cleared.

extra.message: A prop/parameter/identifier value reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no sanitizer. If any of the data on this path is user-controlled (a bio, a comment, markdown, an AI-generated string), this is stored/reflected XSS. Sanitize with DOMPurify.sanitize before it reaches __html, or render the value as text. SCOPE OF THIS CHECK (#1342), so its silence elsewhere is not read as a clean bill of health: it reports the prop or identifier reaching __html. Whether the value was already sanitized upstream — by the component's caller, a shared formatter, or at write time — is outside what this rule reads, so a correctly sanitized value can still appear here.
